prompt: Evaluate $\int_0^1 x\sqrt{1 - x^2} \, dx$. Give your answer as a fraction.
hint: Let $u = 1 - x^2$. Then $du = -2x \, dx$, so $x \, dx = -\frac{1}{2} du$.

hints.text: Let $u = 1 - x^2$. Then $du = -2x \, dx$, so $x \, dx = -\frac{1}{2} du$.
Limits: $x = 0 \to u = 1$, $x = 1 \to u = 0$. The integral is $-\frac{1}{2}\int_1^0 \sqrt{u} \, du = \frac{1}{2}\int_0^1 u^{1/2} \, du$.

explanation: Substitute $u = 1 - x^2$, $du = -2x \, dx$. The $x \, dx$ in the integrand becomes $-\frac{1}{2} du$.
Limits flip: $u$ runs from $1$ to $0$. Flipping them back removes the minus sign: $\frac{1}{2}\int_0^1 u^{1/2} \, du$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Keep $x$ and back-substitute
steps: Either route works; changing the limits avoids the back-substitution.
